note: Sat 14 Nov 2026 run, against Fri 13 Nov US close. Fri was a mixed/narrow session -- Dow +0.10% (52,347.55), S&P 500 -0.4% (7,561.67), Nasdaq -0.9% (25,136.27) -- as Nvidia's post-Huang-resignation slide deepened (NVDA -2.0% on the day, ~13% below its Nov 6 close) and Treasury yields pushed toward 5%; VIX closed 19.30, +3.2% on the day. CNN Fear & Greed mirrors converged well this run (38-40 across three independent sources) vs the prior run's wide scatter -- 39/Fear is used (stockstobuynow.ai and feargreedmeter.com both show current=39, prevClose=40, prev1w=24). Crypto F&G fell sharply to 20/Extreme Fear (from 28/Fear) per alternative.me direct read -- a 4-month low. Under the hood, Friday's breadth was actually calmer than Thursday's rout: NYSE advancing/declining issues were ~44.6%/51.8% (a mild ~1.16-to-1 decliner tilt, vs Thursday's near-3-to-1 decliner day), though new lows still swamped new highs broad-market (~445 lows vs 79 highs per StockCharts/247wallst) and the McClellan Oscillator flipped to -35 (from +1.77 Thu), suggesting momentum is fading even as the headline indices held up. Flows got a genuine refresh this run: both LSEG Lipper and BofA/EPFR published fresh week-ended-11-Nov cuts (vs the prior run's stale 4-Nov vintage) -- global equity funds extended their inflow streak (Lipper: +$50.99B, 7-week high; BofA/EPFR: +$98.3B, most since June, on a broader fund universe), led by Europe (+$35.13B, largest since Jun 2021) and with fresh China (+$2.1B, extending a record 5-week/$88B streak) and Japan (+$4.2B, 5th week) prints from BofA/EPFR. Money-market funds swung sharply from the prior week's +$118.0B inflow to a -$37.5B outflow (Lipper) -- a cash-into-risk rotation that sits awkwardly next to the weakening breadth signal above.
